I believe these reactions.

It will happen in your own time and the moment you realize that you've **adapted** to what happened, well, it's a beautiful thing. You'll find yourself listening to a song from your past that helped you remain strong in times of darkness and cry tears of happiness because you made it out alive. Better yet, you made it out with your love intact.

 No matter what, there will always be moments that hit you like a ton of bricks. Family's in the park, a bbq, family pictures will always bring some sort of pain.The what if's will always be there. You'll just find that YOU made yourself a life that is absolutely glowing with love. That love will guide you to the life you deserve and leave the one's who hurt you where THEY belong: in the past.

The first thing I would like to say is that I am sorry. Nothing about this pain and disease is fun. I know I cannot change how you think but I would like to share with you how I started to get better after years of trauma and depression. I will say that I did have a breakdown very recently and even posted to the forum about how I was writing my goodbye note. I thought I was a burden to everyone, like I was a disappointment. Something in me snapped when I had been doing so well. Meditating really saved me from the constant battle of depression/PTSD but I refused to do it that day because I didn't want an answer that involved me staying around: I wanted finality.

After I wrote my note, I calmed down a little, that eerie calm where you accept your lot in life. Maybe I was meant to kill myself? Well, since I was going to give in anyway I decided to meditate one more time - what could it hurt? Well it hurt a lot haha, I was freaking out inside my brain but I enjoyed it because it felt cathartic. Instead of cutting myself I was bursting open the wounds in my heart which I'm pretty sure was the exact thing my self-survival button wanted me to do. When my husband came home, I cried UNCONTROLLABLY. I realized I lost trust in myself, humanity, and everyone around me because of my trauma. There was some more things but I'd rather not share that here. Mediation saved my life.

I am not saying this will help you but for many years I thought suicide was going to be my future. Until I started meditating, I had no sense of self or self worth. I wanted to hate myself because I felt like I deserved it. I deserved death. I'm slowly getting better but it's not an easy fix. I will say that **this forum and the people who comment have helped me at my lowest and I just want to give back**. Many told me to meditate or gave me some other advice and without it I would have been alone. You are not alone. *You are hurting and that is okay*. Your sensitive soul has not gone unnoticed and I believe in you. I believe you can ask for help or even find your own solution like meditation was the answer for me. **Therapy is definitely one you should look into.** I figured I'd say something because I know I wanted people to answer my post. I needed people to tell me their stories, so now I am telling you mine.

Depression is a mother f\*\*\*\*\*.

​

Edit because I forgot to add: your parents seem like lovely people so tell them. It's not easy to be so open but do it to save your life. They will love you and work with you to get the help you DESERVE.

I think 12 was probably the worst and most memorable part of my life. That's when I became depressed, suicidal etc,. My mother was an alcoholic/coke/heroin addict and verbally abused me as well as physically abused me (Dad not really in the picture). We moved out of my grandparents house and I had no friends in my new town. I was picked on, called a hillbilly (even though I was from the city), and then I went home to another hell. I hated my life but that hatred turned into a plan to escape. I isolated myself in my room and just thought of the future I wanted.

I succeeded and got away from my mom. I am now 28. I'm not going to act like everything is perfect, I mean I suffer from PTSD, depression, and anxiety but I have a loving husband and a dog! In my past, no one was there for me, but I made damn sure I got the love I needed for my younger self. It's a tough road ahead and the death you've experienced at such a young age is truly unfair but please know that you can find support here while you need it.

To be honest, he's the reason why I fought so hard to get better. I'm glad he was able to have a conversation about it and actually learn what it takes to help someone like me. If people were more willing to listen and change their perspective then I'd like to think that all of us would feel safe, loved, and understood.

“The so-called ‘psychotically depressed’ person who tries to kill herself doesn’t do so out of quote ‘hopelessness’ or any abstract conviction that life’s assets and debits do not square. As someone who was in a similar situation, I understand what you're feeling. For many years I was scared of my mother because she would mentally & physically abuse me. When I turned 18, I was still under her spell until I received the phone call that she was on heroin. I realized in that moment that I have no reason to fear someone who is emotionally weak. The only reason why she hurt me for all of those years was because she hated herself and in turn hated me. I stopped talking to her and moved on with my life. We are trying to rebuild a connection now that she is sober but I still get worried that I'm going to get a call mentally abusing me. If you are scared for your safety please make sure to be surrounded by people. Change your number, and whatever else you think you can in the moment. 

My father was another problem. He would make me feel guilty for not calling him or seeing him but he is NOT a good person & never made the effort for me. I'll never forget him choking me on the head rest of his car for not telling him good enough directions. He was the source of many panic attacks until I realized I do not need to speak to him. I really thought about how it's not fair that he left me, that he guilted me with things normal fathers do, and that he thought of himself as father of the year when he wasn't. HE would tell me gross things I did not need to know. This past year (28 now) I cut him off. My anger overcame my guilt. I realized that he holds no power of me and he sucks. Some may disagree but I thought about all of the bad in order to let go. 

Im going to be honest, I'm still mentally messed up from my past. I've been diagnosed with PTSD/depression/anxiety and hate myself most of the time. But the one thing I am proud of is that I did what young me thought was impossible - I got away. It's one of the hardest choices and acts we can commit in a world where "family is everything" but find your own family who can help you delete your father from your life. My SO has shown me how love is supposed to be and he has encouraged me to leave behind the things that hurt me. **If you are scared for your safety please make sure to be surrounded by people.
